title: Yunus's du'a
hookLine: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong (21:87)

lines: A MAN INSIDE A GREAT FISH.
DHU'N-NUN: THE ONE OF THE FISH.
cards: Night. Deep water. And inside a great fish, a man.

The Qur'an doesn't give the size of the fish or how long he stayed. It gives the prayer. The man is Yunus, the one the Bible calls Jonah, and surah twenty-one gives him a nickname: Dhu'n-Nun, the one of the fish.

He had gone off in anger, the verse says, thinking he would not be hemmed in; commentators read that phrase more than one way. Now there is nowhere left to walk. So he calls out from the darkness, in three short clauses.

teach.h: FIRST: THERE IS NO GOD BUT YOU.
teach.b: Surah twenty-one, verse eighty-seven, in Pickthall's translation: "There is no God save Thee. Be Thou Glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer." Look at the order.
First, there is no god but You: before he asks for anything, he says who he is talking to.

teach.h: THEN: GLORY TO YOU, ABOVE ANY BLAME.
teach.b: Second, glory to You, subhanak: You are above any blame.

teach.h: LAST: I WAS WRONG. NO ONE ELSE BLAMED.
teach.b: Third, I was wrong. The Arabic is min az-zalimin, one of the wrongdoers. Its root, z-l-m, gives zulm, injustice, which the classical dictionaries explain as putting a thing where it doesn't belong.
It's the same root as Adam's zalamna, four days ago. And notice what's missing. He doesn't blame his stubborn people, or the ship's crew who cast lots, or the fish.
He doesn't even ask to be let out. The asking is folded inside the admitting.
The next verse gives the answer: Allah heard him and saved him from his distress, and this, the verse says, is how He saves the believers.
Surah thirty-seven adds that if Yunus had not been one who glorified Allah, he would have stayed inside the fish until the day of rising.
A hadith in al-Tirmidhi calls this the du'a of Dhu'n-Nun, and says no Muslim prays with it for anything without being answered.
So Muslims who know it turn to it in tight places: a hospital corridor, a debt, a night that won't end.

how: Some Muslims recite the du'a of Yunus, la ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu min az-zalimin, in times of distress, sometimes many times over, and some gatherings recite it together when someone is in trouble.

o: no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong
save me from the fish and the dark sea
forgive my people, who refused to listen

s: in his du'a, Yunus blames his people for his trouble
he blames no one but himself: I was wrong.
a hadith in al-Tirmidhi says this du'a is answered whenever a Muslim prays with it
it is called the du'a of Dhu'n-Nun.
the Qur'an tells us exactly how long Yunus was inside the fish
the Qur'an gives the prayer, not the length of the stay.

games.q: you are Yunus, in the dark inside the fish. you have one breath to call out. what do you say first?
o: there is no god but You.
my people drove me to this.
games.why: he begins by naming who he's speaking to, then glorifies, then admits: I was wrong. he never even asks to be let out.

practice: Let your breathing slow. If you pray, say the words of Yunus three times, in Arabic if you know them or in English, a breath for each part: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong.
If you don't, sit with the last three words alone, let one small thing come to mind where they're true, and set it down in the dark without arguing or explaining.

wordCard.voice: Yunus's du'a. Three clauses from the belly of the fish: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong. The hadith calls it the du'a of Dhu'n-Nun. Today's word.

orig.s: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
orig.say: laa i-LAA-ha il-LAA AN-ta, sub-HAA-na-ka, in-NEE KUN-tu mi-naz-zaa-li-MEEN
orig.note: Arabic: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was one of the wrongdoers (21:87).

carryVoice: Your line: I was wrong. Said plainly, with no but after it. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: There is no God save Thee. Be Thou Glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer.

Qur'an 37:139–148 (Yunus, the fish, had he not glorified)
